learn.title: Unlink, then free
learn.body: To delete a node, make the node before it skip over it, then free the removed node. You need to remember the previous node while walking, because a node cannot see backwards.

learn.title: Find it, remember the one before
learn.body: `prev` trails one step behind `p`. The loop stops at the match, or at the end if there is none.

learn.title: Unlink and free
learn.body: No match means p is NULL, so the list is returned as it was. Otherwise skip over p, free it and return the head.

learn.title: Deleting the head
learn.body: If the match is the first node, `prev` is still NULL. There is no earlier node to update, so head itself moves to `p->next`. That is why the function returns the new head.

learn.title: Deleting 2 from 1, 2, 3
learn.body: The loop reaches the node holding 2.
steps: p is node 1, prev is NULL, no match. prev becomes node 1
p is node 2: match, and prev is node 1
`prev->next = p->next` makes node 1 point at node 3

learn.body: After `free(p)` do not use p again. Here the function returns straight away.

questions.prompt: Why does deletion need the previous node?
choices: It must be re-linked to skip the removed node
questions.explanation: The earlier node's next has to point past the deleted one.

questions.prompt: What does `remove_value` do when the value is not found?
questions.explanation: Without a match, nothing is unlinked and l is returned as it was.

questions.prompt: Deleting the first node means moving \_\_ to the second node.
questions.explanation: There is no earlier node to re-link, so the head pointer changes.

questions.prompt: The list is 4, 5, 6 and you delete 5. What value comes right after 4 now?
questions.explanation: Node 4 now points straight at node 6.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with calling `free(p)` and then reading `p->next`?
choices: The memory has been given back
questions.explanation: Reading freed memory is undefined behaviour.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to delete a middle node.
steps: Walk until p holds the value
questions.explanation: Unlink first, then free the node that is no longer reachable.
